articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 in late May 2026, featuring substantially improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation within a single model, and a dramatically expanded context window. The model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on graduate-level STEM benchmarks and complex agentic coding tasks, narrowing the gap between AI assistants and autonomous software engineers.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves New Highs on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2 with a specialized math-reasoning mode that scored gold-medal level on a simulated IMO problem set, solving 5 of 6 problems with full formal proofs. The system combines chain-of-thought search with a Lean 4 proof verifier, representing a meaningful step toward AI systems that can contribute to novel mathematical research.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoids in BMW Factories
articles.summary: Figure AI started its first large-scale commercial deployment, placing over 200 Figure 03 humanoid robots across two BMW manufacturing plants in South Carolina. The robots handle bin picking, parts transfer, and quality inspection tasks, operating alongside human workers with an updated vision-language-action model that enables real-time task adaptation without reprogramming.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Demonstrates Autonomous Household Task Chaining
articles.summary: Tesla showcased its Optimus Gen 3 prototype performing multi-step household chores including sorting laundry, loading a dishwasher, and tidying a living room in sequence without human intervention. The demo, while still in a controlled environment, highlighted improvements in dexterous manipulation and semantic scene understanding that suggest a 2027 limited consumer release may be feasible.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude's Tool-Use Orchestration Layer for Enterprise Automation
articles.summary: Anthropic released a new enterprise orchestration framework that allows Claude models to autonomously plan and execute multi-step workflows across dozens of integrated business tools, including Salesforce, Jira, and internal databases. The system includes a built-in audit trail and human-in-the-loop approval gates, addressing key enterprise concerns around AI agent reliability and compliance.

articles.title: ASML Reports Breakthrough in High-NA EUV Yield, Enabling Sub-1.4nm Process Nodes
articles.summary: ASML disclosed that its latest high-NA EUV lithography systems have achieved production-grade wafer yields exceeding 90% at partner fabs, clearing a critical barrier for Intel and TSMC's sub-1.4nm node roadmaps. The improvement was driven by new pellicle materials and advanced computational lithography, potentially accelerating the next generation of AI accelerator chips by 6-12 months.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Approval for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface Trial
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to begin human trials of its N2 implant, which features 4x the electrode density of the original device and a wireless data throughput of 200 Mbps. The expanded trial will include patients with both spinal cord injuries and ALS, with early N1 trial participants already demonstrating the ability to control robotic arms and navigate computer interfaces with high precision.

articles.title: Meta Open-Sources Llama 4 Behemoth with Mixture-of-Experts Architecture at 1.2T Parameters
articles.summary: Meta released the full weights of Llama 4 Behemoth, a 1.2-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates roughly 200B parameters per forward pass. The model matches or exceeds proprietary frontier models on most public benchmarks and is released under a permissive license, intensifying the debate over open-weight AI safety while significantly lowering the barrier for enterprises to deploy state-of-the-art language models on-premises.
